subject: trouble with region.N and multiple sessions

messages.author: 5a91d3696b12d600
messages.subject: trouble with region.N and multiple sessions
parts:
I have a multi-session model with density covariates to model inhomogeneous bear density over a large region.  When I run region.N(model.1), I get the following error message:

Error in getcellsize(mask): mask lacks valid cell size (area or spacing).

I am using 2 different masks (1 for each session) and have tried different ways to define the mask and session for region.N but none have worked.  The Dsurface plots work fine.  Anyone have any ideas on what I am doing wrong?  Thanks for the help and sorry for the cross-posting on phidot.
Joe

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: trouble with region.N and multiple sessions
parts:
Hmmm...

I assume you are constructing each session-specific mask and combing as a list. I get these results for an analogous example:
library(secr)
CH <- subset(ovenCHp, session = 1:2)

msk <- make.mask(traps(CH), buffer = 300, nx = 20)
fit <- secr.fit(CH, model = D~session, mask = msk)
region.N(fit)
# OK

msk <- list(make.mask(traps(CH[[1]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20),
            make.mask(traps(CH[[2]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20))
fit <- secr.fit(CH, model = D~session, mask = msk)
region.N(fit)
# error in getcellsize(mask) : mask lacks valid cell size (area or spacing)

msk <- list('2005' = make.mask(traps(CH[[1]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20),
            '2006' = make.mask(traps(CH[[2]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20))
fit <- secr.fit(CH, model = D~session, mask = msk)
region.N(fit)
# OK

So it seems region.N is unduly sensitive to the lack of names, but there is an easy workaround. The last example still has the problem that the list would not be recognised as a multi-session mask for plot, summary etc. But that would be easily fixed by setting class(msk) = c('mask','list').

Murray

Hmmm...

I assume you are constructing each session-specific mask and combing as a list. I get these results for an analogous example:
library(secr)
CH <- subset(ovenCHp, session = 1:2)

msk <- make.mask(traps(CH), buffer = 300, nx = 20)
fit <- secr.fit(CH, model = D~session, mask = msk)
region.N(fit)
# OK

msk <- list(make.mask(traps(CH[[1]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20),
            make.mask(traps(CH[[2]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20))
fit <- secr.fit(CH, model = D~session, mask = msk)
region.N(fit)
# error in getcellsize(mask) : mask lacks valid cell size (area or spacing)

msk <- list('2005' = make.mask(traps(CH[[1]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20),
            '2006' = make.mask(traps(CH[[2]]), buffer = 300, nx = 20))
fit <- secr.fit(CH, model = D~session, mask = msk)
region.N(fit)
# OK

So it seems region.N is unduly sensitive to the lack of names, but there is an easy workaround. The last example still has the problem that the list would not be recognised as a multi-session mask for plot, summary etc. But that would be easily fixed by setting class(msk) = c('mask','list').
